TASK ID: subset-sum-to-partition

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum to Partition. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Subset Sum and TARGET is Partition. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = SubsetSum
Subset Sum.

Instance: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
  * The numbers are non-negative integers of any size; values may repeat.
  * The target is any integer.

Yes iff some sub-list of the numbers (each position used at most once)
sums to exactly t.

Edge cases: t = 0 is always yes (the empty sub-list). t < 0 is always
no. An empty list is yes only for t = 0.

TARGET = Partition
Partition.

Instance: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...]}
  * The numbers are non-negative integers of any size; values may repeat.

Yes iff the positions can be split into two groups whose numbers have
equal sums (every position goes in exactly one group).

Edge cases: an empty list is yes (two empty groups). An odd total is
always no. Zeros never change the answer.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-wk3d5e7n
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above. It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.
Do not merely describe code: leave the files at those exact paths.
Every reply must contain exactly one bash tool call. When you are done, finish by running exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-wk3d5e7n && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum to Partition.

Source instance (Subset Sum):
    {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
Target instance (Partition):
    {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...]}

Construction
------------
Let S = sum(numbers).  Append the single number

    b = abs(S - 2 * t)

and output {"numbers": numbers + [b]}.

Why it is correct
-----------------
The new total is S + b and a valid partition needs a subset summing to
(S + b) / 2.

* t < 0: b = S - 2t, so the new total is 2(S - t) and the required half is
  S - t > S.  No subset of the original numbers can reach it, and adding b
  only overshoots, so the Partition instance is "no" -- matching t < 0.

* 0 <= t <= S/2: b = S - 2t >= 0, total = 2(S - t), half = S - t.
  A group summing to S - t either contains b, forcing the rest of that group
  to sum to t, or does not, in which case its complement (containing b) sums
  to t.  Hence Partition is "yes" iff some subset sums to t.

* S/2 < t <= S: b = 2t - S >= 0, total = 2t, half = t.  A group summing to
  t either excludes b (a subset sums to t) or includes b (the rest sums to
  S - t, which exists iff a subset sums to t, by complementation).  Hence
  Partition is "yes" iff some subset sums to t.

* t > S: b = 2t - S > t, so a group summing to t cannot contain b, and
  without b no subset of the original numbers reaches t > S.  Partition is
  "no", matching Subset Sum.

* t = 0: b = S, total = 2S, half = S, always achievable (all originals vs b),
  matching the always-yes edge case.

Zeros and the empty list are handled by the same formula.  The construction
uses only a sum and an absolute value, so it runs in linear (polynomial) time
and never calls a solver.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Return a Partition instance yes iff the Subset Sum instance is yes."""
    numbers = instance["numbers"]
    target = instance["target"]
    total = sum(numbers)
    extra = abs(total - 2 * target)
    return {"numbers": list(numbers) + [extra]}
EOF

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum to Partition.

Source instance (Subset Sum):
    {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
Target instance (Partition):
    {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...]}

Construction
------------
Let S = sum(numbers).  Append the single number

    b = abs(S - 2 * t)

and output {"numbers": numbers + [b]}.

Why it is correct
-----------------
The new total is S + b and a valid partition needs a subset summing to
(S + b) / 2.

* t < 0: b = S - 2t, so the new total is 2(S - t) and the required half is
  S - t > S.  No subset of the original numbers can reach it, and adding b
  only overshoots, so the Partition instance is "no" -- matching t < 0.

* 0 <= t <= S/2: b = S - 2t >= 0, total = 2(S - t), half = S - t.
  A group summing to S - t either contains b, forcing the rest of that group
  to sum to t, or does not, in which case its complement (containing b) sums
  to t.  Hence Partition is "yes" iff some subset sums to t.

* S/2 < t <= S: b = 2t - S >= 0, total = 2t, half = t.  A group summing to
  t either excludes b (a subset sums to t) or includes b (the rest sums to
  S - t, which exists iff a subset sums to t, by complementation).  Hence
  Partition is "yes" iff some subset sums to t.

* t > S: b = 2t - S > t, so a group summing to t cannot contain b, and
  without b no subset of the original numbers reaches t > S.  Partition is
  "no", matching Subset Sum.

* t = 0: b = S, total = 2S, half = S, always achievable (all originals vs b),
  matching the always-yes edge case.

Zeros and the empty list are handled by the same formula.  The construction
uses only a sum and an absolute value, so it runs in linear (polynomial) time
and never calls a solver.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Return a Partition instance yes iff the Subset Sum instance is yes."""
    numbers = instance["numbers"]
    target = instance["target"]
    total = sum(numbers)
    extra = abs(total - 2 * target)
    return {"numbers": list(numbers) + [extra]}
